correctness.rationale: For p=2 and exactly three nonzero active coordinates, Yang–Yuan Proposition 11 leaves only I={2,3} in \psi_u(\lambda_1) and only I={1,2} in \psi_u(\lambda_3). Direct cancellation gives \psi_u(\lambda_1)/\psi_u(\lambda_3)=((\lambda_3-\lambda_2)/(\lambda_2-\lambda_1))(u_3/u_1)^2. Combining this with the primary paper’s delayed endpoint recurrence yields R_{k+2}=C R_{k+1}/R_k^2. Proposition 3’s fixed-weight conjugacy multiplies C by w_3/w_1. Centering at R_*=\sqrt C gives z_{k+2}=z_{k+1}-2z_k, whose roots (1\pm i\sqrt7)/2 have modulus \sqrt2. The nonzero recurrence has unbounded states and cannot remain one-signed for more than a bounded run, forcing both positive and negative unbounded subsequences and hence R limsup infinity and liminf zero. The bundled decimal replay is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The final claim is already a direct special-case implication of the exact primary theorem under the required implication standard. Yang–Yuan give the delayed recurrence, prove that every nonterminating p=2 three-mode block has all three active coordinates, give the complete Cauchy–Binet endpoint formula in Proposition 11, and give the fixed-weight conjugacy in Proposition 3. Substituting n=3,p=2 and r=1,3 makes one term survive at each endpoint; one line of cancellation produces the submitted ratio recurrence, and solving its elementary second-order log recurrence produces the \sqrt2 law. Because special cases and corollaries count as covered even when the paper does not print the resulting wording, the absence of the ratio theorem as a named proposition cannot support originality.
